title: 1950 AHSME Problem 36
statement: A merchant buys goods at \(25\%\) off the list price. He desires to mark the goods so that he can give a discount of \(20\%\) on the marked price and still clear a profit of \(25\%\) on the selling price. What per cent of the list price must he mark the goods?

solutions.text:
Let the list and marked prices be \(L\) and \(M.\) The merchant’s cost is \(0.75L,\) while the selling price after the discount is \(0.8M.\) A profit equal to \(25\%\) of the selling price means that the cost is the remaining \(75\%\) of that price. Therefore \[ 0.75L=0.75(0.8M)=0.6M. \] Thus \(M=1.25L,\) or \(125\%\) of the list price.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Take the list price to be \(L\) and the marked price to be \(M\)
The cost is \(0.75L,\) the selling price is \(0.8M,\) and the cost is \(75\%\) of the selling price
